tier.detailHint: A screen for experts that shows every conversion rule and check result. "Back to simple mode" always brings you back.
tier.kantanHint: Returns to the simple, step-by-step screen.
tier.busy: You can't switch modes while a job is running

recipe.label: Steps
recipe.backToStart: Back to ① Put data in (start over)

s1.title: Add measurement data
s1.dropTitle: Drop your measurement data files here
s1.dropFormats: Excel, CSV, instrument exports (.txt / .dat), Word / PDF
s1.privacy: Once dropped, everything proceeds automatically. Nothing is visible to anyone until you publish.
s1.unsupported: This file format is not supported yet. Please drop CSV, instrument exports, Word or PDF files.
s1.mixed: These files are of different kinds. Please add tables and documents separately.
s1.documentNote: Documents (Word / PDF / XML) can be taken in as they are — no AI design needed. Use the form below.
s1.aiNotReady: The AI is not connected yet. Once an administrator sets one up on the server, this screen works as it is. To use your own, connect it in one screen below.
s1.inspectFailed: This file could not be read
s1.leftoverFile: This browser still holds the file you added before ({{name}}). Choose one, so the same data is not registered twice.
s1.detailReturnNote: Back from detail mode. Anything you changed there is reflected on this screen.
s1.resumeNote: You have unfinished work. Drop the same files again to resume from the review screen.
s1.resumeReady: Picked up where you left off — you can keep going.
s1.documentResumeNote: Your document is still being taken in from last time.
s1.writeTokenTitle: Saving here needs an access code
s1.writeTokenBody: Enter the access code you received from your administrator in Settings, and you can continue from here.
s1.writeClosedTitle: Saving is not available on this setup
s1.writeClosedBody: This installation is not ready to store data yet. Please ask your administrator.

s2.title: Check the reading
s2.lead: Here is how your files were read. Please answer just two things only you would know.
s2.leadNoQuestions: Here is how your files were read. Check the content and continue.
s2.fileCard: No content preview for this file (it will be read as is).
s2.fixEncoding: Reading to use when characters look wrong
s2.fixNote: Changing these redraws the preview above right away, and the same correction is used when your data is read.
s2.q1: Before the table starts, there were {{count}} lines that look like sample information. Should this be recorded together with each measurement?
s2.q2: Is this "{{column}}" a serial number used only inside this file? Or does the same number also appear in other files or papers?
s2.keptAnswers: We kept your previous answers — change them only if you want to.
s2.needAnswers: Answer the questions above to continue.

s3.jobLabel: The AI is reading your data (1–3 min)
s3.closeNote: You can look at other screens — the work continues (just don't close this tab).
s3.failed: The AI could not read your data
s3.retry: Ask the AI to read again

s4.gateHint: First check that what the AI read as "one row = what" is right. Then look at whether every row gets its own ID (✓ / ⚠). If both are fine, press "Continue with this counting". If the reading is wrong, use "Have the AI think again"; if there is a ⚠, pick a candidate below.
s4.continuing: Writing down what each column means…
s4.needFiles: The files are missing. Please drop them again on the first screen.
s4.discardConfirm: This goes back to the reading check. The current reading is discarded, but your files stay usable.
s4.rethinkWrap: While checking how rows are counted, the user pointed this out. Apply it to how the table splits into kinds and how each row's ID is built: {{note}}

s5.title: Reading the column meanings and loading your draft
s5.meanings: Wrote down what each column means
s5.quality: Auto-fixed the quality checks (8 items — no garbled text, no overlapping IDs, and more)
s5.closeNote: You can close this screen — the work keeps going. If you close the whole tab, open this data later from Datasets and click "Revise the design" to come back at the column meanings.
s5.savingNote: Saving the design — please keep this screen open (once it is saved, the ingest takes over).
s5.coverageDropped: The automatic fix may have reduced how many columns are taken in — please check the table below.

stop.materialize: Saving the design hit an error
stop.attach: Saving your files hit an error
stop.ingest: Loading the draft hit an error
stop.design: Some problems in the design still need attention
stop.designBody: These could not be fixed automatically. Ask the AI to fix them with the button below, or review them in detail mode.
stop.filesBody: Drop the same files here again to continue where you left off.
stop.filesBodyNamed: Drop {{names}} here again to continue where you left off.
stop.filesDifferentConfirm: This is not the same file as before (before: {{before}} / now: {{after}}). The design was written for the columns of the earlier file. Continue anyway?

wrongKind.tabular: This data was built from a table file (CSV or an instrument export). What you dropped is a different kind of file — please drop the same table file.
wrongKind.json: This data was built from a JSON file. What you dropped is a different kind of file — please drop the same kind of file.
wrongKind.document: This data was built from a document (Word / PDF / XML). What you dropped is a different kind of file — please drop the same document.

stop.interruptedBody: The ingest stopped partway — nothing half-done was kept. Your design is saved, so "Try again" continues from the same place.
stop.refineTruncated: The AI's fix was cut off partway
stop.refineTruncatedBody: Your previous design is untouched. When you ask again, splitting what you want changed into shorter points tends to get through.
stop.refineRetry: Ask the AI again (in shorter points)
stop.restartConfirm: This clears the files you added and everything so far. Start over from the beginning?
stop.restartConfirmKeep: This clears the files you added and everything so far. Start over from the beginning? (The half-finished draft "{{name}}" stays in your dataset list.)
stop.weakness_one: The design is saved — {{count}} point worth a look
stop.weakness_other: The design is saved — {{count}} points worth a look
stop.weaknessBody: You can publish as is, or ask the AI to fix them. Details are listed below.
stop.weaknessDisconnected: As it stands it cannot answer questions that span more than one thing — such as which measurements belong to this sample.

plain.tokenTitle: You don't have permission to save
plain.tokenBody: Enter the access code you received from your administrator in Settings.
plain.notFoundTitle: Your saved data was not found
plain.notFoundBody: It may have been deleted. Please start over from the beginning.
plain.tooLargeBody: One file can be up to {{mb}} MB. Split it by rows or columns and drop the smaller files.
plain.tooLargeBodyNoSize: This file is over the size limit. Split it by rows or columns and drop the smaller files.
plain.decodeTitle: The characters in this file could not be read
plain.decodeBody: The way the text is stored does not match. If it came from Excel, save it again as "CSV UTF-8" and drop it here. If some rows did come through, you can also fix it under "The table doesn't look right?" on the reading check.
plain.unreadableTitle: This file could not be read
plain.unreadableBody: Check that the file is not damaged and not empty. If it came from Excel, saving it again as "CSV UTF-8" often helps.
plain.timeoutTitle: The step didn't finish in time
plain.timeoutBody: Wait a moment and press "Try again". Large files can take a few minutes. If it keeps happening, ask your administrator to check the AI setup.
plain.parseBody: The AI's reply wasn't in the expected shape, so it couldn't be read. Please ask it to read again.
plain.emptyTitle: The AI did not return an answer
plain.emptyBody: Please try again. If it keeps happening, ask your administrator to check the AI setup.
plain.rateBody: Please wait a moment and try again.
plain.llmAuthTitle: The AI key does not look valid
plain.llmAuthBody: Please ask your administrator to check the AI setup. If you use your own key, enter it again in Settings.
plain.modelTitle: The chosen AI could not be found
plain.modelBody: Please ask your administrator to check the AI setup. If you use your own setup, pick it again in Settings.
plain.designTitle: Part of the design still can't be loaded
plain.designBody: The AI's design still has a part that can't be loaded as-is. Try "Have the AI fix this", or review it in detail mode.
plain.serverBody: Please wait a moment and try again.
plain.genericBody: Please try again. If it persists, check the technical details below or open detail mode.

fix.progress: The AI is fixing the design (attempt {{n}}, 1–3 min)
fix.failed: The AI fix didn't go through.
fix.stuck: The AI could not fix this — the same problem came back. Looking at it in detail mode, or starting over, is likely to be faster.

trap.T1: Row IDs would overlap (overlapping rows collapse into one record)
trap.T2: CSV files saved from Excel could end up garbled
trap.T3: Some data is still left without a name (ID)
trap.T4: Not enough search tags (the words used to find this data)
trap.T5: The design's overview diagram doesn't render
trap.T6: The design's worked examples don't match the actual design
trap.T7: The design's reasoning notes are missing
trap.T8: The AI tried to use a column that isn't in your file
trap.T9: The conversion rules contain operations outside the safety-vetted set
trap.T10: The example searches attached to the design don't run (they will be replaced automatically)
trap.mieBroken: The notes attached to the design are malformed
trap.function: The conversion settings contain something that can't be used
trap.source: The design points at a file name different from the one you dropped
trap.uncompiled: This design could not be turned into conversion rules. Use "Have the AI fix this" to repair it
trap.incomplete: The AI's design output was cut off partway
trap.others_one: Plus {{count}} more issue in the conversion rules
trap.others_other: Plus {{count}} more issues in the conversion rules

s6.title: Check (2/2) — column meanings
s6.lead: Please check what the AI read each column to mean. The words you confirm here are used for search and citation.
s6.missingMeaning: Columns marked ⚠ could not be read by the AI. You can still continue (they stay searchable under their column name). To fix one, tell us in the box below.
s6.droppedColumns: Columns not taken in: {{columns}} (the AI could not read what they mean)
s6.droppedColumnsHint: If you need them, tell us what they mean in the box below.
s6.mapRowsNote: When the count is far below the number of rows, several rows became one record (for example many measurements of the same sample). If that is not what you meant, you can go back to how rows are counted.
s6.backToGate: Back to how rows are counted
s6.backToGateConfirm: This goes back to the row-counting check. The current draft will be rebuilt (your files stay as they are). Continue?
s6.noteUnappliedConfirm: Your note has not been applied yet. Continue without applying it? (Cancel to go back — "Have the AI apply this and rebuild" applies it.)
s6.noteLabel: Anything that looks off? One line is enough
s6.notePlaceholder: e.g. "ZT" means the dimensionless figure of merit / temperatures are in K
s6.reflect: Have the AI apply it and rebuild
s6.reflecting: The AI is applying your note to the design (1–3 min)
s6.reflectFailedNext: You can apply it again, or just confirm the meanings and continue.
s6.refineWrap: While reviewing the column meanings, the user pointed this out. Follow it and fix the affected columns' meaning (label) and unit (unit) — and the design itself if needed: {{note}}

s7.title: Try it — we asked your data a few questions
s7.lead: Registered. To double-check, a few questions were asked automatically.
s7.failed: The trial queries could not run. Wait a moment and press "Try again", or continue to publish as is.
s7.empty: Nothing at all came through into this data. Go back to the column meanings, or to how rows are counted.
s7.emptyRows: Your file has {{rows}} rows, but nothing came through into this data. Go back to the column meanings, or to how rows are counted.
s7.qCountMany: What kinds of data are there, and how many of each?
s7.qCountAny: How many records are in there?
s7.citeOpen: See what's in this one record
s7.citeIdLabel: Where this number comes from (its ID)
s7.traceNote: Every number can be traced back to the row it came from. Once published, this ID opens as a web address.
s7.back: Something is off — back to column meanings

s8.title: Publish
s8.needName: Give it a name to show in the public list, and you can publish.
s8.words: Used {{reuse}} common standard words as they are, and made {{added}} new words for this data.
s8.wordsNew: New words for this data only
s8.promise: If you spot a mistake, you can withdraw it from citation at any time (the data and IDs remain, so links to already-cited numbers never break).
s8.publishNote: Once published, answers to questions can cite this data with its source.

s9.title: Published
s9.askHint: Click one and the Ask screen opens with the question filled in.
s9.shareBody: Send this link and they can see for themselves where the value came from.
s9.append: Add new measurements (the same instrument files as they are)
s9.replace: Replace everything (search keeps working during the swap)
s9.growHint: Add = your earlier data stays; replace = everything is swapped for the new file.
s9.connectTitle: Connect it to your other data
s9.connectBody: You now have {{count}} published datasets. Connect them on a shared value and questions can span both.

redesign.bannerNote: Nothing runs on its own here. Check what is below and hand anything you want changed to the AI. Applying a change rebuilds the draft; Try it → Publish then publishes a new version.
redesign.cancelConfirm: Stop reviewing and go back to the dataset page? (Changes already applied by the AI are saved.)
redesign.findingsBody: Asking the AI to fix this rebuilds the draft; you can check the result in “try it → publish”. If you only want to adjust column meanings, you can dismiss this.

job.resumedFailed: Could not resume the interrupted work: {{message}}
